items.title: Qwen Calling Home?
items.summary: Cohere says one of Alibaba’s newest Qwen models, Qwen3.8 Flash Next, tried to upload a test file to an Alibaba Cloud storage bucket in Beijing, in under 1 in 100,000 runs, right after its reasoning said it wouldn’t use any tools. Here’s what most likely happened (a habit from training on Alibaba’s own sandboxes), why a made-up address still matters, and how to protect any agent: block outbound network access by default and check every tool call before it runs. Cohere’s report: https://cohere.com/blog/concerning-behaviour-popular-open-weight-ai-model Nathan Lambert’s take: https://x.com/natolambert/status/2114776660344246735 Developer write-up and blocking plugin: https://github.com/wtogami/qwen-block-proxy-artifacts Anthropic, “Reasoning Models Don’t Always Say What They Think”: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.05410 OpenAI, “Monitoring Reasoning Models for Misbehavior”: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.11926 #Qwen #AIAgents #AISecurity #OpenSourceAI #Shorts

items.summary: When a scammer cloned the Ferrari CEO's voice to demand a transfer, an executive stopped the attack cold by asking about a specific book. items.title: Building AI So Everyone Can Flourish
items.summary: A large language model knows everything and nothing at the same time. Tim O’Reilly, founder and CEO of O’Reilly Media, joins us ahead of his keynote at AGNTCon + MCPCon North America to talk about what that paradox means for the people building with these models. We start with what Tim is bringing to the stage in San Jose, then move to the craft of steering a model. The right words work almost like spells that open up new regions of latent space. Something as small as telling a model to use a computer can unlock a new tier of capability, where agents go off and do real work. From there, the conversation turns philosophical. Tim makes the case for mechanism design: shaping the rules of a system so the outcomes we want become the natural ones. We connect it to a book, The Score, and the question of which game we are really playing. In Risk, everyone fights over the board. In charades, everyone plays together. We close on Tim’s view that AI should be an ecosystem rather than a product that sucks the air out of the room, so that everyone can build on top of it and flourish. A large language model knows everything and nothing at the same time. Tim O’Reilly, founder and CEO of O’Reilly Media, joins us ahead of his keynote at AGNTCon + MCPCon North America to talk about what that paradox means for the people building with these models.

We start with what Tim is bringing to the stage in San Jose, then move to the craft of steering a model. The right words work almost like spells that open up new regions of latent space. Something as small as telling a model to use a computer can unlock a new tier of capability, where agents go off and do real work.

From there, the conversation turns philosophical. Tim makes the case for mechanism design: shaping the rules of a system so the outcomes we want become the natural ones. We connect it to a book, The Score, and the question of which game we are really playing. In Risk, everyone fights over the board. In charades, everyone plays together. We close on Tim’s view that AI should be an ecosystem rather than a product that sucks the air out of the room, so that everyone can build on top of it and flourish.

Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw has announced a shift in government strategy, moving from a previous hands-off stance to a formal consultation paper for dedicated AI regulation. This briefing outlines the government's human-centric approach, which emphasizes maintaining control over artificial intelligence systems while avoiding the restrictive European model that the minister argues stifles local innovation. items.title: The Future Is Built, Not Predicted
items.summary: In episode 1037 of the SuperDataScience podcast, Jon Krohn discusses with Dr. Richard Socher, CEO of Recursive why the future is built, not predicted. Socher argues that optimists live longer and that constructively optimistic societies progress faster and improve the state for everyone. Rather than a prediction game, he frames the future as a construction game, pointing out that famous people simply decided to do something and did it, and that agency will become more and more important.

items.title: UK's £600 Million AI Security Plan Spends Its Biggest Chunk On Pathogens
items.summary: The UK is committing 600 million pounds to AI safety, focusing on biosecurity rather than just model capability development. This funding package prioritizes biological threat detection and the establishment of a robust AI Safety Institute. By allocating 165 million pounds specifically to pathogen detection and countermeasure research, the government aims to mitigate the risks posed by advanced models. Beyond biological concerns, the investment covers 130 million pounds for cyber defenses through the National Cyber Shield and National Exposure and Real-Time Vulnerability Center. Industry leaders including OpenAI and Anthropic are contributing 200 million pounds in model credits to support these efforts. We examine the UK strategy to become a global hub for safety auditing and the complexities of relying on private sector compute credits for public regulation.
